Game seems like it could be a good time. However, from week 1, to week 2, the rent goes from roughly 1.5k to 50k. The tutorial really doesn't teach you much in regards to how to properly expand, and meet these metrics. I'd say its a pretty large learning curve. The curve isn't how the style of the game presents itself. I'm happy with steep learning curves in games like Factorio. The difference here is, the run is over if you can't make the rent payment. Definitely could be a fun game, if I wanted to minmax a little farming simulator game.

The rogue-like aspect seems to be only based off of unlocking other professions and such instead of per-run iterative improvements, which is disappointing. That being said, I think the game is fun and worth it for the low price.

Oh this is a wonderful little game to tinker with. I will say that the sheer variety of options/produce/zones to buy might give some people choice paralysis but as long as you go in with a focus depending on which class you pick, you should be fine. I can vouch that easy mode is seriously easy. I'm interested in trying the harder difficulties in the future but right now my main goal is to do an endless easy modem run and make the cutest farm you ever did see. KEY POINTS - Tutorial is VERY light. At a minimum I'd like to have seen a prompt for the Crafting screen and how to upgrade a tool. - Be prepared to spend a lot of time clicking through the inventory/crafting/building tabs to read through what you can do. That said, the crafting recipes shown on mouse-over of any inventory item is very helpful. - You can get produce very easily - the main challenge is balancing other resources in order to process them sustainably for the highest sell price. Farting through my first farmer run, I had 200 parsnips but I was coal-less and glass-less, so I ended up offloading them for cheap because I'd already gotten a much higher crop. - Inventory navigation is awkward due to volume of items and the short hotbar. Sorting options are focused on price, not the type of item. - Currently the game can give you unwinnable challenges (e.g. build a fence in one day but you don't have the level to build a fence). That kind of thing can tilt out new players.

[h2] A Fast-Paced Farming Rush! [/h2] This is farming on a timer, and it works surprisingly well. You’re not here to chill, you’re here to build, grow, craft, and pay your rent (unless you're in endless mode, then you're free to throw off the shackles of real life in your video game). Another Farm Roguelike: Rebirth is a mix of roguelike systems and frantic farming in a way that’s fun, addictive, and slightly chaotic. There’s no combat to distract you, just pure strategy: what crops to plant, which upgrades to choose, and how to earn enough to beat the rent and complete your challenges. If you’ve ever wanted Stardew Valley but at 3x speed and with more spreadsheets in your brain, this might be your thing. ✅Smart roguelike systems tied to farming ❌Feels rushed if you prefer slower pacing ✅No combat, just clever time/resource management ❌Rent mechanic might stress out more casual players (switch to Endless mode) ✅Challenges and perks keep each run fresh 👉Read my [b] full review [/b] here: [url=https://www.screenhype.co.uk/another-farm-roguelike-rebirth-review-strategic-farming-without-the-frills/] Another Farm Roguelike: Rebirth Review – Strategic Farming Without the Frills [/url] https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eooNnmuPmeA&ab_channel=ConversingwiththeStars

This game has one of the steepest learning curves I’ve encountered in any roguelike and unfortunately, it does very little to guide you through it. The mechanics are poorly explained, leaving new players frustrated and lost. On top of that, the game suffers from serious balance issues that make progress feel inconsistent and sometimes unfair. The user interface is also lacking polish and can be quite clunky to navigate. With some major improvements, it could have potential, but in its current state, it’s a frustrating experience. Solid 4 out of 10.

I feel like another farm rougelike: rebirth actually might be worse than the first one for like two main reasons. 1. The fact that there's only 2 or 3 weeks in each mode is a really crazy change. This completely prohibits you from achieving a satisfying build without going on endless (which you can but you've already won so it doesn't matter (to me at least)). Easy and normal are two weeks and are both stupidly easy but for hard and crazy they ramp up the rent so much it almost seems impossible. this is because they devs insist on keeping the 2 or 3 week count so the only way they can make it harder is by upping the rent. This makes the game feel more like a puzzle game rather than a rougelike as you have to do specific things in a specific order. Also having the game be so short doesn't even make sense since you wont even be able to build certain things since you aren't a high enough level. 2. This game seems VERY unbalanced. the original was a slightly unbalanced too but this one is WAY worse. I haven't even tried a majority of the builds in this game but unless your doing a clothing build (which takes a while to set up due to levels anyways) you won't have enough time to really set up. 2 weeks is barely enough time to make 50k and absolutely not enough time for 80k. Even if you do manage to get all the materials you need to build or make something this game has levels which block the building off until you get enough exp. this means you HAVE to wait to be able to start up your build which makes it a lot harder to get a build running quick enough to meet rent. These two thing really kill the game as you don't have enough time to mass produce the lower priced objects enough to meet rent which leads you to either lowering the difficulty to be super easy or repeating the same build over and over again which is like the worse crime to commit as a rougelike. It feels like the devs made a longer rougelike and like their publisher or someone held them at gun point and forced them to add the 2/3 week count instead of the normal 5/6 one. This game has a bunch of content that you will not use in the main mode because it is just way too short. if there would be one thing I'd beg the devs to change it would upping the week count. THIS GAME IS NOT MEANT FOR 3 OR 2 WEEKS PLEASE CHANGE IT BACK THE GAME WOULD BE 1000x BETTER. This game has such good bones but the week count just really kills it.

AFR:R revisits some of the mechanics from the previous AFR and evolves them into a true roguelike style. There are multiple ways to complete a level, and you often need to adjust your playstyle depending on your level, the biome, the level-up powerups, or the missions. I wouldn’t recommend it if you’re the kind of player who just googles the fastest way to make money—because that won’t always work here (unless you reset every run until you get the perfect starting conditions). This is a game that needs to be learned and tested thoroughly before you can stand a chance at higher difficulties. Personally, I think that’s the beauty of it. I’ve logged over 50 hours, just unlocked the last class, and have completed 9 challenges and 3 crazy difficulty runs. Before writing this, I read some other reviews and I’d like to clarify a few points: The game has never crashed for me, not even with 500+ animals or when closing it (for reference, I play on a mid-to-high-end PC). I agree that 2–3 weeks is too little to fully take advantage of the farm, which always feels a bit rushed (unless you go into endless mode after winning). Some complained about the 60 FPS cap, but honestly, I don’t see the point of 144 FPS if the animations only have 60 frames anyway. The game will let you fail many times before you get results, but at the same time, it offers multiple paths to victory. Different classes also open the door to different playstyles, which keeps things fresh. One thing I wish it had is an in-game wiki (at least for the biomes). Once you unlock an island, there’s no way to check what that biome does—unless you still have another island of the same biome locked. TL;DR: The game is great, with a steep learning curve. I highly recommend it. It’s both relaxing and challenging (sometimes too challenging on crazy mode). I’ll definitely pass 100 hours of gameplay, and for just £5, that’s better value than most AAA titles.

Update 2: Honestly I tried the game more. The below still stands but I need to just add that the game wont let you enjoy it unless you enjoy digging into each and every smaller action you can take and mostly why you shouldnt have taken it. The game feels unfairly designed towards the player unless they enjoy pain Also, while I understand this is tongue and cheek: "Wait, Farming Can Actually Be Satisfying?!". This does still feel like a dig at farming simulators especially with what follows after where it literally talks about the social aspect of those games. As if its a downside. An optional... feature is a downside and hinders satisfaction I guess. If you need to put other games or people down to elevate your game, chances are your game is sh**e. Sorry not sorry, Dev. You took the first one and the overengineered it to the nth degree where its no longer fun. The Gloves are off. I dont care anymore. This game is what it is. Update After playing it again and the prequel by comparison I cannot recommend this game in any way shape or form. If you dont min max this game you wont get anywhere. The game now requires you to be a master at strategy from week one and if you even dare go into any other difficulty above normal, you will feel like you are playing Chess against the highest level bot there is. --- [strike]I will give this game a thumbsup for one single reason: The devs clearly put in a ton of love and effort into the sequel. And that alone I shall reward. That being said, I will now go into heavy critique as I am coming from the prequel.[/strike] - The game feels overcomplicated, more so than the first one. You have now regions to unlock which is fine until its not You now need to level up in order to unlock recipes for buildings which is fine until its not. - The main problem is that its basically trying to make you min max. Which you already have done with the previous game but now it forces you into purely minmaxing for level gain. Tools now have to level up in order to be upgraded - Which means it doesnt matter if you have all the ore and ingots readily available, good job on that, you still have to wait and waste precious stamina. You feel railroaded into discovering and understanding convoluted mechanics which do try to expand on the first game which is great until its not. - If you play this for the first time, it will overwhelm you. If you play this as a player of the old game it will overwhelm you. Cause there is a LOT to keep track of. A lot to take in. A lot to understand right from the start. Here is for instance a big issue I have with the current state of the game and then I go into nitpicks: - You are no longer in control of your own stamina drain and will almost always close the day with at the very least 1 stamina left. This is agonizing cause you have no way to spend that stamina. - The earliest form of consumable, being fruits, can indeed be consumed for stamina now. 3 times per day. And they give you like 4 stamine each. Yes you can make them into drinks and more which is great! Until you realize that the only two out of three fruits give you worthwhile drinks starting out and the rest is just for money. - You now have multiple ways to generate Ores. You have the wood mine. The stone mine. The Desert Mine. The Mountain Mine. And probably more that I dont realize or havent gotten to yet. All of which give you different ressources. Pray tell: Why? Why do we have 4 ways to generate practically the same ressources? Why are diamonds (Which was dependant on high RNG and a bonus before) available like every other Ore now? - The Challenges/Quests you get in this game feel so random at times that you think to yourself "Aight we skipping this one. And this one. And this one. And t- can I like get one that I can manage what is this??" How am I supposed to: Gain 300 XP or roll 50 times in the store on week one?? In 3 days?? - You now have the oportunity to shape yoru week. Thats cool. Until you realize that on a bad card draw it doesnt matter and none of the careds will help you in a meaningful way. Yes this is already similar to how it worked previously. Just with the added bonus of you being able to choose your own bad cards over just being given some by the RNG gods. - The Tutorial you get can cover stuff you need to take care of. Such as selling items from your inventory. Which is behind the tutorial window. --- Nitpicks: - The UI is TOO BIG - I cant zoom in or out - I can no longer re-arrange my inventory (granted that is not a bad change but now I need to scroll throw every inventory bar till I get to my tools. Which takes a while when you have gathered a lot of items already. - I cannot use the Escape button to close minor windows or any window to return to the main gameplay screen. - Right clicking an item makes a pop up appear. The Minor windows in question. Which I can only close by hitting the top right X button of said window. Why is this a thing? - The game feels like it was designed for Mobile Gaming. And that makes me actually a lil bit disapointed.

[h1] 「♥另一个肉鸽农场♥」 [/h1] [h2] 「♥游戏介绍♥」 [/h2] 另一个肉鸽农场是一款模拟经营+建造类的肉鸽游戏，玩家可以选择不同的职业，利用每个职业的技能效果来选择对应的玩法，种田，钓鱼，挖矿，烹饪，畜牧等等各种各样的经济来源，选择各种各样的增益事件和减益事件，完成限时任务，升级选择强力技能，让自己的农场赚到越来越多的钱，哦对了，记得按时交租金嗷，不然游戏就结束了，休闲玩家也可以选择不需要租金的无限模式，体验休闲农场的乐趣。 [h2] 「♥游戏内容♥」 [/h2] 游戏的玩法上大致是分为两种的，一种是正常模式，玩家要按时交钱来保证自己的生存，有个目标才有动力思考每天要做什么，但是有的玩家不想看着自己辛苦经营的农场倒闭，那么也可以选择不要租金的无限模式，没有任何压力的去经营一个农场，或许更适合。 说回正常模式，玩家一开始要选择自己的职业，选完职业后就相当于奠定了本局游戏的基调，决定了一整局的流派玩法，然后选择3个增益buff和3个减益buff，记得选择对自己有利的，BUFF会按照天数进行轮换，轮换完所有的buff之后会开启新的一轮选择buff时间，总之选择对自己的职业有利的就可以了。 玩家在完成各种工作之后都会获得经验值，每次升级的时候可以获得强力技能选择机会，这个选择是真很强大的，一定要慎重考虑，有的时候可以突然暴富，逆转即将暴毙的命运。花费金币解锁新的地块，每个地块都有自己的特点，解锁的顺序也很重要，先找对自己有利的地块解锁。 [h2] 「♥总结♥」 [/h2] 另一个肉鸽农场是一款将各种种田相关的玩法融入到一个小地图中，再加入肉鸽和生存的要素，形成了一套完整的体力规划和建筑规划的玩法，推荐给喜欢种田类工作和肉鸽的玩家进行游玩。 [table][td]欢迎关注鉴赏家[url= https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45519015/]“无趣评测”[/url][/td][/table]

[h1]肉鸽来相助，种田很轻松！[/h1] 相对于星露谷来说，这个种田的节奏是很快的。上手也是比较容易的，游戏很好地把种田和肉鸽的玩法充分地结合起来，特别推荐玩无尽模式，种起来特别爽。 [h3]游戏玩法 [/h3] 本作的内容简直可以说是量大管饱，有着丰富的职业，甚至每一个职业中还细分三个子职业，都有不同的等级收益和技能效果。不过开局只有三个大职业，后续的很多大职业逐渐解锁。挑战模式有相关的难度，经典模式的话每周的地租还会暴涨，他们都要考虑好策略，不过肉鸽升级的三选一随机性和轻松的鼠标点击足以弥补这一点。种田的话和其他的游戏没有什么太大的区别，玩肉鸽游戏起来还是很上头的。 不过游戏还有一些可以改进的地方，第一没有联机模式，孩子什么都会干的呀。第二强行减益有点恶心，哪怕是最简单的。因为有着交租金的压力，每过一周上涨得比较快。难度是和时间挂钩的。第三有功夫的话可以优化一下 UI。还是略显复杂的。不过综合来讲的话是利大于弊的，也算是发挥出了肉鸽种田游戏的特色，是值得一玩的。 [h3] 结语[/h3] 什么？种田游戏居然能和肉鸽的结合起来，另一种肉鸽农场是一个快节奏的策略种田游戏，只需通过鼠标的轻松操作来赚取足够多的钱来应对持续上涨的地租。从小块土地出发，逐步地解锁八种不同的生态地区，建造独属于你的特色农场！肉鸽充分地结合到这个游戏的每一个特性之上，几十种种不同的角色，每升一级随机获取技能，地图资源随机生成，有着丰富的建筑和道具。推荐游玩无尽模式。体验更轻松！快来体验独属你的种田时光吧！ [quote]关注「[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45580968] 月の赏 [/url]」[/quote] [u][b] 月揽千游，一赏知味 [/b][/u]

I’m not going to deny my absolute love of management sims. There is, for me, something deeply cathartic about making a plan, designing out an approach, gathering the resources, and doing it. I like seeing the end result and having the satisfaction of not only a plan well-executed, but of then getting to build that plan further and further into grander and grander things. I used to be a project manager, and I hated it. I’m sure there’s something to analyse there about my psyche, but this is a review of Another Farm Roguelike, and let’s be honest, neither of us wants that particular analysis. Another Farm Roguelike: Rebirth is exactly what it says on the tin. It’s a farming-themed roguelike where players design and build a farm, planting crops, raising animals, and earning money to pay an ever-increasing rent. There’s something to be said about the fact that, even in a management fantasy, we are all still beholden to the capitalist demon that is the rental economy, but that is, again, not the point, and no one but me wants that. It is worth getting one obvious truth out of the way from the outset. This is a game heavily inspired by, if not a vague parody of, Stardew Valley. Its graphics, its sprites, its mechanics are all very familiar to anyone who has played any amount of Stardew. Eggs go into the mayonnaise machine, milk into casks, fruit into the juicers, and all the products get sold to invest back into the farm. There is very little about the particular chain of production that is unfamiliar here, to a point that it feels vaguely uncomfortable in how blatant it is. This is not, however, Stardew, as evidenced by the fact that the presence of rent necessitates building not a whimsical, fun farm that might have optimisation if the player playing wants that, but rather, a capital engine. This is a game that’s very much an optimisation challenge, even if it buries the lede a bit on that being the case. Much of how Another Farm Roguelike presents itself centres around it, first and foremost, being an anti-Stardew, with it repeatedly emphasising how much it does not feature the “cosy” elements of Stardew. I’m going to admit that this particular approach of denigrating another, perfectly lovely game rubs me the wrong way, though none of this is necessarily the fault of the game itself. Bad marketing doesn’t mean the game itself is bad, as any fan of the Dragon Age series can attest. More deceptive, though, is the game’s emphasis around player choice and diverse strategies. Another Farm Roguelike, the game’s page argues, is all about having a diverse range of play experiences. Each map is randomly generated, each segment within the map has random resources within it, all leading to the player being nudged to try a variety of different approaches to the problem of paying rent. Except none of that is true. Yes, there are a range of biomes, and yes, resources are random, and absolutely, there are a variety of starting bonuses the player can choose from, but fundamentally, each run of Another Farm Roguelike has one of two outcomes—the player either has the map layout to build an efficient farm, or they lose after two or three weeks. There is no middle ground. Much of the problem of Another Farm Roguelike is that, while it presents the idea that there are many valid ways to scale and grow a farm, in practice, there are not. The fact that rent grows exponentially while the farm’s engines grow linearly means that there will quickly come a point—usually after the second week—where it is physically impossible for the farm to raise enough money to make rent. This is, of course, unless the player has had both phenomenal luck in their map generation, the correct class to make the best use of the map, and the knowledge of what specific plays to make in order to best make use of what they’ve been presented with. What this creates, then, is a roguelike in the worst sense. Rather than growing and learning from each playthrough, and unlocking the tools to make the next playthrough easier, the player is beholden to the whims of the RNG, with no real chance of making a run with a bad RNG work. The other aspect of this flaw is that, once a player does understand how to win and what to look for in a map, there is very little reason to replay the game. Since the number of truly scalable strategies is so limited, the only winning move is to repeat what works for a given class ad infinitum until it’s just boring and trite. The worst thing a roguelike can be is repetitive. The game, to its credit, does offer a potential solution to the rent problem in the form of an “endless mode.” Endless mode removes the rent requirement entirely, allowing players to just build a farm to their heart’s content with no external pressures. To which I ask: then what’s the point? The entire premise of the game, everything it promises and everything it wants to be, is a challenging farm management sim. Take away the challenge, and all you’re left with is a knockoff Stardew that’s missing any sense of charm. This is the tragedy of Another Farm Roguelike: Rebirth. There’s a lot here to like. It’s satisfying to build a strategic farm, and the idea of having a range of biomes and layouts does add refreshing variety to each playthrough. However, when that variety is undergirded by the knowledge that building this farm is a Sisyphean task, much of the fun of it all is lost. What’s the point in building if none of it is ever going to be enough? [h1]一切创意都在探索之中的肉鸽农场，欧~或许简单难度入门正合适[/h1] 入门门槛，极高！我说不小心点到最高难度开一把的玩家，那租金嘎嘎高，水温烫的不行🙅‍非常不建议刚上手的玩家直接尝试，也暴露出来一点：《另一个肉鸽农场》的机制非常负责，加上引导性较弱，全靠社区里的攻略口口相传深挖游戏里的各种机制，笔者入坑时得到了以下大大的帮助，排名不分先后，也希望各位能得到帮助： https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3538639254 https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3542467065 以及一些爱好者WIKI与外站帖子的帮助： https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3545242465 看了这几份攻略，假如你对赛博老农之路上还有任何问题，欢迎帖子下留言！ 此外也对游戏做个简单介绍和评测喵： 作为一款非常特别的将“肉鸽”元素与“种田”元素结合的模拟经营类游戏，用类似于空岛生存的形式，随机为玩家安排了一个个富有特色的“荒岛”进行开垦活动，基于此玩家利用各种手里的资源与随机的天赋搭配进行“种地”，并应对逐渐上涨的租金！ 而游戏里玩家天生自带精力系统与一个“平凡职业”，在辛勤耕地，砍树，挖石头，钓鱼（其实有点偏向于中期了）的过程中消耗精力，获取经验，并不断升级获取新天赋——然后继续赚米，再滚雪球，再更多大米！ 对于该游戏来说，隐藏在后台里的“背包”“商店”“建造”“制作”“数据”等一开始会令人头大，但是结合7天一轮回的次数累计，大概能摸索出来这个游戏的尿性：滚雪球滚得越大，钓鱼钓得越爽，当你一切战术转钓鱼佬的时候，会发现一片新天地！ [quote] 闲暇时光，不妨试试游戏。 欢迎关注[url=store.steampowered.com/curator/45653622/] 闲暇時光鉴赏组 [/url] [/quote]
